text:
aisha_ae: quick heads-up — FinSys wants a POC for a private deployment. Security wants no public ingress, egress must be allowlisted, and they need source IP preservation for their on-prem firewall. Asking for guidance: PrivateLink vs VPC peering? NAT/EIP requirements? any blocking ports? also need rough pricing delta between Dedicated and Private for initial sizing.
rob_se: thanks — can you capture a few quick constraints? are they multi-account? traffic volumes? regulatory egress allowlist vs dynamic domains?
aisha_ae: single AWS account today, might be multi-account later. Expected steady 50 rps, bursts to 200. Need fixed egress IPs for allowlist. Regulated fintech (PCI scoped), so audit logs and KMS required.
devon_arch: high level: PrivateLink (AWS NLB + VPC endpoint) is easiest for cross-account isolation and avoids route table changes. Good when you want fixed endpoint in their VPC and to keep your infra in our VPC. VPC Peering/TGW gives lower latency and full VPC connectivity but more network blast radius and complicated cross-account setup.
devon_arch: short pros/cons:
- PrivateLink: no transitive routing, per-service VPCE, easier allowlist (they allow outbound to our VPCE private ip ranges), integrates with NLB.
- VPC Peering/TGW: higher throughput, lower latency, but requires route propagation, potential overlap checks, and more security review.
matt_netops: about source IP preservation — if they need to see original client IP on prem, you need to avoid NAT on the egress path. Typical patterns:
- Use their NAT/Egress GW with static EIP -> preserve source by routing traffic back (requires static EIP set on our side or proxy)
- Use a customer-managed proxy in their VPC (eg an outbound forward proxy) and configure our requests to go via that proxy
- If we egress from our private deployment, we can assign Elastic IPs to NAT Gateways in their VPC or ours (but NAT will translate source)
rob_se: for allowlist, simplest: they give us a small set of EIPs to use. If they want domain-level allow, we provide FQDNs like `*.redwood-inference.com` (but some firewalls can't do wildcard TLS inspection). Also can publish a short-lived list of IPs if they accept periodic updates.
aisha_ae: what about firewall ports? any special ports apart from 443/80?
devon_arch: mostly 443 outbound. If using PrivateLink via NLB, you need healthcheck ports on the NLB target group (usually TCP 443 or TCP 8000 depending on our agent). If they plan TLS inspect, ensure SNI/passthrough works. Example minimal egress snippet for their firewall:

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood endpoints
- Protocol: TCP
- Ports: 443
- Destination: 10.10.50.0/24 (VPCE subnet) or <list of EIPs> (if NAT/EIP)
- Description: Redwood Inference private endpoints
```

matt_netops: if they require fixed outbound IPs for our side, we typically recommend they host a small outbound proxy (curl+nginx) in their VPC with an EIP and we route traffic to it (then they can whitelist that EIP on their downstream partners). Otherwise, we can reserve EIPs on our side but that'll require a peer agreement.
rob_se: pricing: very rough (ballpark for initial scoping) — Dedicated: committed GPU pool, predictable monthly cost; think in increments (example) ~$18k/month per 8xA10G or similar (includes infra + platform markup). Private: platform license + customer infra — expect a platform fee (one-time + annual) e.g. $20k-$50k depending on support + they pay for infra (EC2/GPU + networking). Need exact quote from finance for the deal.
aisha_ae: thanks. I'll flag finance for an official quote. any blockers we should surface in the presales call?
devon_arch: blockers:
- overlapping CIDRs (peering/TGW) -> demand unique CIDR from customer
- strict egress rules that disallow any dynamic updates (we can work with them but may need ops-run cadence for IP rotation)
- requirements for inbound private traffic to our management/control plane (we can offer customer-managed control plane or VPN for admin)
matt_netops: also confirm KMS/HSM expectations and audit log retention. If they require an airgapped control plane, that's a separate Private offering.
aisha_ae: next steps: I'll schedule a 30m tech-handoff with FinSys + their netops. @devon_arch @matt_netops can you join tomorrow 10am PT? I'll attach their security questionnaire beforehand.
devon_arch: can do.
matt_netops: ok for 10am PT.
infra-bot: reminder: create tech-handoff calendar invite and upload security questionnaire to the shared drive
aisha_ae: uploaded questionnaire and a quick network diagram in the thread. I'll also request their preferred egress IPs list before the call.
rob_se: perfect, I'll prep a one-pager comparing PrivateLink vs Peering + rough cost bullets for finance.
aisha_ae: thanks all :raised_hands: — will update after call.
